name: Customer tracks an order
summary: A returning customer opens their past orders, drills into one, and tracks its shipment. The journey is honest about the two states a real account hits: a customer with no orders sees an empty state, and a paid-but-not-yet-dispatched order shows a 'tracking not available yet' state rather than a fake delivery stage. Reuses the same Plant / Customer / Order dataset as the buy-a-plant flow (extended, not duplicated).

steps.label: My orders
steps.human: The customer sees a list of their past orders with number, item, total and status.

steps.label: Order detail
steps.human: The customer opens one order to see item, quantity, total, payment status and date.

steps.label: Track shipment
steps.human: The customer sees the current delivery stage for the order — the carrier, tracking number and where the parcel is (shipped / in transit / delivered).

branches.label: No orders yet
branches.human: A customer who has never ordered opens 'My orders' and sees a friendly empty state inviting them to browse the catalogue, rather than an empty table.

branches.condition: the order is paid but not yet dispatched (stage 'not-shipped', no tracking number)
branches.label: Tracking not available yet
branches.human: The order has been paid but not yet handed to the carrier, so there is no tracking number: the customer sees a 'not shipped yet — tracking will appear once it's on its way' state instead of a fake delivery stage.

acceptance_scenarios.then: each order shows its number, item, total and status

acceptance_scenarios.given: a customer who has never placed an order
acceptance_scenarios.then: an empty state is shown inviting them to browse the catalogue, with no order rows
the order detail shows item, quantity, total, payment status and date

acceptance_scenarios.given: a paid order that has been dispatched
acceptance_scenarios.then: they see the carrier, tracking number and the current delivery stage for that order

acceptance_scenarios.given: a paid order that has not yet been dispatched (no tracking number)
acceptance_scenarios.then: they see a 'not shipped yet' state explaining tracking will appear once the parcel is on its way, and no fake delivery stage is shown

provenance.note: Second seed flow; reuses fern-and-fig/catalog to demonstrate extend-not-duplicate + the flow selector.

v2: added the no-orders empty-state branch and the tracking-unavailable (paid-but-not-dispatched) branch so the flow stops assuming every account has a shipped order. The track step now reads the Order shipment fields (carrier / tracking_number / stage) added to the catalog dataset in the same pass. Set realization=mock.
